The Story

Today's Snow Reporter

Friday, Nov. 20, 2026:

It's been a great week up here! Snow is falling all the way down in town as I write on this Friday afternoon. There's 20 inches of natural snow piled up at the summit, and the past few days have been cold enough to make lots more snow mountainwide!

We're scheduled to kick off the 2026/27 ski season on Friday, Dec. 4 — just two weeks away — and we're stoked to see you all back on the slopes. So start planning your next visit today! Lift tickets, frequent skier cards, lessons, daycare and on-mountain lodging are available now.

Planning to ski or ride before opening day? Please note we've entered the two-week preseason period described in our uphill policy, which means you must stay on the East Route between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m.

The Benny Up Route and all other parts of the mountain are off-limits during those hours, for both uphill and downhill travel, every day for the next two weeks. No exceptions!

Our teams have a lot of work to do to prepare for the season ahead — driving snowcats, moving goods and equipment, making snow and potentially throwing explosives for avalanche mitigation. All of these activities pose serious risks to skiers and riders who get in the way. It's imperative for everyone's safety that we avoid surprise encounters on the slopes.

Additionally, please park in the Spruce Lot near the Base Lodge, keep your dogs leashed at all times, and immediately clean up after them if they do their business on the skin track.

For more information, please review the full uphill policy and route maps. We appreciate your cooperation!

The snow report is a subjective assessment of terrain and weather conditions. Snowfall and snow depths are measured at the summit and base areas around 6 a.m. each day. Actual depths may vary across the mountain and change throughout the day.

If you go out of bounds ...

When you exit the marked boundaries of the resort, you are entering backcountry terrain where natural and human-caused avalanches can occur. The resort does not conduct avalanche mitigation on those slopes. Always check the Flathead Avalanche Center's daily avalanche forecast and carry a beacon, shovel and probe.
